name: Step-Back Prompting
executive_summary: Have the model first step back to derive a high-level concept or principle from the specific question, then use that abstraction to guide the actual reasoning — abstract before you solve, rather than solving directly.
description: Targets a distinct failure mode from Problem Elaboration Prompting's context-clarification focus: rather than clarifying what a question is asking, Step-Back Prompting has the model first derive the general principle or first-principle concept underlying the specific instance (e.g. asking 'what physical law governs this?' before solving a specific physics problem), then reasons through the specific question guided by that abstraction. Tested with PaLM-2L, GPT-4, and Llama2-70B, with substantial gains on STEM, knowledge QA, and multi-hop reasoning — for example, +7% and +11% on MMLU Physics and Chemistry, +27% on TimeQA, +7% on MuSiQue for PaLM-2L.
when_to_use: Questions that are instances of a more general principle or concept (physics, chemistry, knowledge-QA, multi-hop reasoning) where identifying that principle first would make solving the specific instance easier.
when_not_to_use: Questions with no useful higher-level abstraction to step back to — purely computational or lookup-style tasks.
known_pitfalls: If the model derives the wrong abstraction (an incorrect or irrelevant general principle), the specific-instance reasoning that follows is misguided by a bad premise.

primary_source.authors: Zheng, Mishra, Chen, Cheng, Chi, Le, Zhou
primary_source.title: Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in Large Language Models

variables.name: stepback_question
variables.description: The generated higher-level question abstracting away instance-specific details

variables.name: derived_principle
variables.description: The general concept/principle the model derives

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
